text: AI-powered cultural archive for India's architectural memory
A working system for digitization, OCR, search, maps and source-grounded research
HackCult '26, Problem Statement 2. The working prototype claim is supported by the deployed frontend and automated test suite. Image source is recorded in frontend/public/images/sites/ATTRIBUTION.md.
The problem and what the system must achieve
Heritage evidence exists, but its formats and archives cannot work together.
Photographs lack metadata. Scanned documents hide their text. Field notes and regional records remain disconnected from the monuments they describe.
Durable private storage and authorized downloads
PDF extraction and OCR for scanned sources
Sites, documents, images and map coordinates
Open browsing, filtering and grounded answers
Problem and requirements come from the hackathon brief and the implemented HeritageLens workflow. No size, accuracy or adoption claims are made.
HeritageLens turns scattered sources into a usable archive
The judges can inspect the deployed product, not a mock-up.
Site metadata plus extracted and corrected document text
PDF extraction, Tesseract OCR and curator correction
Coordinates connect monuments to archival records
Screenshot captured from https://heritage-pearl.vercel.app/. Features are verified in frontend routes, backend services and automated tests.
What judges can experience in the prototype
The deployed product covers public discovery, archival digitization, curator control and source-grounded research.
Search site metadata plus extracted and curator-corrected document text
Filter the archive by period, architectural style and region
Open site records with galleries, metadata, linked documents and original downloads
Explore backend-provided coordinates through an interactive Leaflet map
Upload PDF and image sources with type and size validation
Extract selectable text with PyMuPDF or scan pages with Tesseract OCR
Track processing, review, approval and failure states, then correct transcriptions
Require curator authentication for uploads, edits and deletions
Ask a grounded assistant that returns archive sources and a local fallback answer
Keep originals in configurable private storage with authorized download routes
Show preserved local records when a live request is temporarily delayed

Implemented features verified from frontend routes and pages, API client methods, FastAPI routers, storage and extraction services, curator security, search service and assistant service. The slide describes current capabilities only.
From an uploaded source to verified discovery
Automation handles repetitive processing. Curators retain editorial control.
The backend records errors, preserves the original source and can resubmit interrupted background work after restart.
Workflow verified in backend document router, storage service and background processing service. Upload polling and curator review are implemented in the frontend UploadPage.
The repository uses one modular backend with clear boundaries for storage, processing and public discovery.

The current system can support a controlled institutional pilot. Each feasibility claim has evidence and a defined next step.
Deployed React and FastAPI application with PostgreSQL, private storage, OCR and automated migrations
Run live storage and migration checks after every production deployment
Curator authentication, review states, audit events and recoverable processing failures
Replace the shared prototype login with individual curator accounts
Managed Vercel, Render and Supabase services keep the pilot infrastructure small
Measure storage, OCR time and database usage with real institutional collections
The modular monolith separates API, storage, processing, search and presentation concerns
Move OCR jobs to a managed queue when upload volume exceeds one worker
Ready for a controlled pilot. A broader rollout still needs individual curator roles, production monitoring and a managed job queue.

Feasibility is framed for a controlled pilot rather than a full institutional rollout. The architecture and repository support each current-build claim. Live Supabase storage and production migrations still require deployment verification. Cost claims are qualitative because production usage data is not available.
Who benefits and what comes next
Current pathways: archival OCR and geospatial discovery. Planned pathways: multilingual intelligence and computer vision with 3D experiences.
Find evidence across sites and digitized records
Preserve originals and approve corrected text
Publish structured collections with traceable sources
Explore monuments through maps and accessible narratives
Add individual curator roles, monitoring and a managed OCR job queue
Extend OCR and translation for Devanagari and regional-language sources, then add hybrid retrieval
Ingest crowdsourced monument photographs, reconstruct digital twins and present them in a WebGL viewer
HeritageLens makes cultural evidence searchable without losing the path back to its source.

The current product implements the archival OCR and geospatial pathways described in the HackCult brief. Multilingual OCR and translation, semantic retrieval, crowdsourced photogrammetry, 3D reconstruction and WebGL digital twins remain future work and are not presented as implemented.
